free_tier.stated: no free tier; SSD VPS 1 is USD 2.33 a month billed USD 28 a year

retention.stated: the VPS persists while the annual term is paid; the plan page states no deletion clock
retention.notes: annual billing is the headline; whether a monthly cycle exists on this plan was not shown

interface_detail: root SSH on a KVM VPS with 1 IPv4 and 3 IPv6 addresses
tooling: any SSH client; the deploy endpoint is a per-plan app URL
chaining: the cheapest fully dual-stack VPS with its own IPv4 and no port tricks, so a WireGuard endpoint needs no vendor cooperation
binding_note: 4 TB a month is generous for a personal tunnel and is the only metered thing on the plan; the disk and the 1 GiB of RAM do not bind.

identity_cost.detail: adding a debit or credit card to the billing profile places 'an authorization fee of usually about $1 USD' against the card, which is 'automatically refunded within 7 days'; the hold attaches to adding a card, not to creating the account. 'We support all major credit and debit cards available to date', so a debit card is accepted. A card is one route and not the only one: Cloud Credits can be funded by PayPal, AliPay, card on file or a promotional code, and PayPal and AliPay need no card. No minimum top-up amount is published. The account creation form itself was not read.

confidence_note: price, shape, bandwidth and address count quoted from the plan page read; the payment rails, the debit acceptance and the USD 1 authorisation hold are quoted from three first-party help-centre articles read. The account creation form was not read, so whether the signup itself demands a card is unverified.

notes: USD 28 a year divided by 12 is USD 2.33 a month, which is the vendor's own figure, and USD 28 is the money out of pocket. This is above the USD 1 line and is recorded because it is the cheapest verified machine that needs no shared address and no port forwarding at all. A WireGuard listener on UDP 51820 works on any port here because the IPv4 is dedicated. Payment: the USD 1 authorisation is real and first-party, but it is a card-verification fee placed when a card is added, not a signup deposit, and it is refunded automatically within 7 days rather than on request. The money actually spent on the plan is non-refundable. Whether the signup flow itself requires a card was not established: the account creation form was not opened, and the help-centre articles describe the billing profile after an account exists. RENEWAL PASS 2026-10-24: the annual figure is the standing product price, not a promo, so the renewal is the same USD 28 absent a notified increase. the provider do permit that increase at the start of a renewal term on 45 days' notice, and the agreement auto-renews for the same term unless cancelled at least one day before expiry. The two SSD VPS records now carry the same renewal treatment; the SSD VPS 1 record previously left renewal_usd null while SSD VPS 2 carried it, although both are priced the same way on the same page.

extras.price_arithmetic: USD 28 a year divided by 12 = USD 2.33 a month, annual prepay; a VPS bills whether it runs, so 10 h/day and 24/7 are the same bill
extras.ipv6_prefix: 3 IPv6 addresses, not a stated routed prefix; whether one of them is a /64 is not stated on the plan page
extras.renewal_note: the page prices the plan as 'Billed $28 per year', a standing annual rate rather than a discount off a higher monthly list, so the same USD 2.33 is the recurring charge. It is not locked: the provider let CloudCone raise the fee at the start of any renewal term on 45 days' notice, and silence is deemed acceptance.
